question: Which edit grouping and replay rules preserve user intent, and can competing history owners be removed?
trigger: The owner objected to writing `void editor.api.history.undo()`, asked whether to disable the floating-promise lint, and asked for a harsh first-principles best-api-review of async editor operations: whether an async history API is dangerous for synchronous expectations and whether to support it at all. This scope was closed by the 2026-10-04 Stop; it is not the unit `next` returns.
requirements: One user-visible undo and redo order across document edits and comment-thread creation: Undo C/B/A, Redo A/B/C (TaskHub-22 AC1, AC2).
A refused, stale, thrown or concurrent comment replay leaves the branch head in place and never skips B to A (AC4, AC5); comment persistence stays server-first (AC7).
Public updates are synchronous and cannot nest (docs/vision/plite.md); undo is documented as one complete editor update.
Callers can still observe the true settled outcome of a replay that waits on an external owner (the 2026-09-23 owner request: truthful async completion, pending state, no editor lock).
Every Cmd+Z, toolbar and model call has one result and error owner; no rejection goes unobserved.
Keep typescript-eslint no-floating-promises effective; a gate is not weakened to get green.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-10-04 audit, the 2026-09-23 async-replay, lifecycle and authoring reviews and the TaskHub-22 plan as history. Rechecked on the live tree: history-plugin.ts replay, applyReplay and replayNow; editable-dom-runtime.ts replayHistory and dispatchHistory; keyboard-input-strategy.ts; BaseCommentsPlugin.ts replayCreation and commitMutation; oxlint.config.ts; the history guide and React hooks docs; and a census of every history.undo/redo call site. New: two Bun probes on HEAD source (history-timing.log and settle-failure.log in docs/research/probes/2026-10-05-history-replay-result/, the second confirming a stuck-pending defect after a settle-step throw) and a source survey of eleven editors plus VS Code (survey.tsv beside it).
summary: Pursue: keep the claim, pending, busy and settlement lifecycle, but return a synchronous HistoryResult from editor.api.history.undo() and redo(), with a pending variant that carries a never-rejecting settled Promise. Do not turn off or allowlist the floating-promise lint. The Promise carries nothing for a document batch. The probe shows the text already reverted when undo() returns, and the guide says ordinary batches settle immediately. It still taxes 275 void and 91 await call sites, while all 6 production callers discard it, and an owner throw behind void undo() is an unhandled rejection (probe: 1). The one async case already claims the head and publishes pending before its first await, so a synchronous pending result describes it exactly and keeps every TaskHub-22 law. Mounted Cmd+Z then repairs focus in the call instead of after a forced microtask with focusin and pointerdown guards. No surveyed editor returns a Promise from undo; VS Code returns Promise<void> | void for file operations only and never rejects. The deeper cut, making comment-creation undo local-first and deleting the lifecycle, matches Liveblocks and BlockNote but reverses TaskHub-22 AC5 and AC7, so it stays the owner's product call.

callSites.current:
void editor.api.history.undo();
const result = await editor.api.history.undo();

reconciliation.reason: Its lifecycle, pending state, busy overlap, mounted dispatcher and Plate adapter verdicts stand. It kept Promise undo and redo because synchronous success would lie for a pending comment replay; a synchronous pending result does not claim success, so only the public return channel reopens.

alternatives: Keep Promise<HistoryResult> and turn off or allowlist no-floating-promises: rejected. The Promise is decorative for document batches, misleads void callers that read state right after the call, and the lint reports a real unhandled-rejection path from a throwing owner.
Synchronous HistoryResult with a pending variant carrying settled: strongest target. Same information, honest timing, no caller ceremony, no lint exception, lifecycle unchanged.
HistoryResult | Promise<HistoryResult>: rejected again. Callers must test for a thenable; a status discriminant is the narrowing they already do for busy and blocked.
Separate undoSync and undoAsync methods: rejected. Callers must know the hidden batch kind before calling.

Comments owns in-flight removal optimistically and history becomes fully synchronous with no pending or busy: strongest deletion, matching Liveblocks and BlockNote. It reverses TaskHub-22 AC5 and AC7, so it is the owner's product call, not this review's default.
Remove comment creation from document undo entirely: rejected. It drops TaskHub-22 AC1 and AC2.
proofLimits: Source review, two Bun probes on HEAD source with controls, a source-only editor survey and a design arena (Opus, gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-sol; Opus cross-judge); no prototype of the proposed types, test suite, browser, device or benchmark run. Product comment-undo behavior in Google Docs, Notion, Figma, Linear and Confluence is unverified. The arena's detailed contract (root result types, a failed settlement reported to the lifecycle error sink, synchronous owners settling in the call) lives in the plan and awaits its panel.
